what_it_does: validates workstream records against people.yml team membership and returns a list of error strings

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: the three lowercase sets are rebuilt once per workstream from `people_data['teams']`, which never changes inside the loop; hoisting them above the loop does O(W*T) set builds once instead of per workstream. Read nowhere else; no error text changes

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: `parent_kind` is assigned and never read; removing the line drops a dict lookup and a .get per workstream with a parent. Behaviour identical (id_to_workstream[parent_id] is already known present)

decisions.label: c
decisions.why: a memoised walk would need extra state and the cycle error is reported per workstream in order; depth is tiny in workstreams.yml, no clean small edit

what_it_does: aggregates job records per (repo, workflow file, workflow name) and renders a Markdown table

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: `runs` set duplicates the keys of `run_totals`; dropping it removes one set insertion per record and the `runs` set allocation per group. n_runs becomes len(run_totals), same value since both are keyed by run_id and updated together. Lambda factory is local to this function

what_it_does: pulls every completed workflow run and its jobs through gh, keeping bare-metal jobs as records

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: `parse_iso(started)` (datetime.fromisoformat plus str.replace) runs three times per kept job and `parse_iso(run_started_at)` once per job although constant per run; parse once. Exceptions (ValueError) must still be handled at the same points

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: each run needs its own jobs call; no API shortcut that returns the same data, so nothing to repair

what_it_does: reconciles existing voter comments with the roll file, deleting or patching stale comments (dry-run prints) and posting new batches

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: per stale handle `remove_handle_line` builds a regex and scans the body; k stale handles cost k full scans plus k compiles. One combined pass over the body removes them all with the same per-line pattern

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: `extract_mentions(c['body'])` is run in the tagging pass and again in the stale pass for the same body; computing once per comment halves the regex scans of unchanged bodies. A different edit from `a`, same function

what_it_does: returns True if the first line of a comment body equals HEADER

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: for any body that does not contain HEADER the first line cannot equal it, so `HEADER not in body` returns False without building the list of lines; most issue comments are not voter comments. Return value identical

what_it_does: deletes the `* @handle` line(s) from a comment body

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: re.compile on an identical pattern string hits the re module cache after the first call; no work removed. Any real saving is the combined pass already recorded in sync(a)

what_it_does: pages through a repo's issue comments since cutoff and records, per user, the PR and issue numbers commented on (cached per repo)

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: `number not in <list>` scans the user's whole list for each comment; a local set of seen (user, kind, number) keeps the lists (and their order) but makes the duplicate test O(1). `commenters` lists are consumed only through `_check_comments`, which still receives the same lists

what_it_does: inserts a member entry into the sorted Emeritus section of a README, creating the section if needed

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: each section line is run through `re.match(r'^[-*+] \[', l)` twice (collect member_lines, then find first/last index); one pass that records both removes half the regex matches

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: re module caches the patterns; the per-call cost is a dict lookup, not worth an edit

what_it_does: edits each repo README in memory for every inactive user and opens a PR or issue through the GitHub API

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: removing the rescans means caching parsed sections across a README that is mutated by each user, touching four helpers and the header_level side effect; that is a rewrite, and the unit is dominated by network calls

what_it_does: returns which maintainers have comment, review, authored-PR or merge activity on the given repos

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: reordering changes which activity kind the DEBUG output attributes a user to (reviews vs authored) and the set of requests made; the printed output is part of the contract

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: the second `_check_comments` runs on the already reduced `remaining` over cached dicts; merging the passes changes debug message order and gains little

what_it_does: returns the first matching event per remaining actor from the cached repo events

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: an early break needs a count of matching users in `remaining`, extra bookkeeping for a scan over an in-memory list that is already linear and cached; gain is marginal and input-dependent

what_it_does: renders one README table of SIGs (name, meeting time, invite group, slack, details link)

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: extract_row_data builds ten fields including the people loop with person_link and f-strings, none read here; giving extract_row_data a flag that skips the people block and passing it from render_group removes that work per SIG. extract_row_data is called only from render_group and render_sig_details (grep), and render_sig_details keeps the default

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: `content +=` on a local string is resized in place by CPython; no saving, per the measured string-concat counterexample in verifying.md

what_it_does: renders the details bullets for one SIG

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: avoiding the recompute needs a cache shared between render_group and this function, which would make repeated unit calls look free; the edit lies outside the unit's own contract and is not attributable here

what_it_does: looks up the GitHub login for every devstats name and returns [login, contributions] rows

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: get_github_login calls `requests.get` once per name; a module-level `requests.Session` reuses the TCP/TLS connection instead of a handshake per user. Needs the network to measure
